Loop engineering · experiment 2 · plan for review

Fastwork Loop v2

Rebuild the fastwork.com homepage as MUI parts behind flags, count the work the engine does on every change, put Lean first for everything reproducible (it runs in fwcore, Lean generates it, or the code must pass Lean golden vectors) and show it as math, and save the iPhone for calibration and feel.

Why v2

v1 worked. The loop around it was expensive.

The first experiment made the homepage scroll smoothly on the iPhone. It also took ten days, hundreds of agents and a phone for nearly every measurement.

584 → 42 mslongest frame at the end of the page
≈ $11.4klist-price token cost over 10 days
442agents started (848 transcripts, 2,521 commits)

Pain pointWhat v1's data showsv2 answer

Patching minified SvelteAbout 349 commits on the end-of-page line alone; a replace-all silently broke six SVG circles.React rewrite as pluggable MUI parts. Each part has a faithful variant plus ablation, optimized and proposal variants chosen by flags.

Every decision, queue and status view that can be proved lives in one Lean program, fwcore; TypeScript moves data. Results are cached by content hash, so a tool change re-runs only that tool.
Chat forensics · 848 transcripts · 135k model requests

The agents did their work. The loop around them did not.

Reading every v1 transcript showed one overloaded lead at the centre of everything. Recurring check prompts woke it most of the time, and idle agents lost their cache and paid to rebuild it. The user ended up as device technician and status relay, and agents spent a tenth of their tool turns keeping the console up to date by hand.

10.9%of all v1 tool turns did nothing but write or poll the console (13,279 of 121,286)
56%of the 4,412 hand-written status writes recorded something a machine knew or will know in v2
0console fields an agent can set in v2 (target); every agent input is a typed, refusable request (V-t)

Biggest costs and problems

  • Idle agents losing their cache: 2,924 cold rewrites cost $2,763 (24%).
  • 19 agents alive over 24 hours cost 36% of all spend.
  • 57% of 5,393 errors were worktree refusals of inline shell scripts.
  • 139 of 276 incidents came from the project's own tooling and guards; 4 from agent mistakes.
  • 82–105 of 166 user console steps were device chores; one re-plug waited 11 h 41 min.

What worked and stays

  • Console steps, Try-it proposal pages and comment buttons (median 10 min to a decision).
  • Short, fresh agents: 645 agents under an hour cost only 11%.
  • Message delivery (0.35% failed) and fast replies.
  • One lander with fast-forward-only merges: 0 merge commits in 2,521.
  • A/A noise floors, pinned baselines, prediction cards before data.
The core idea

A two-speed loop

The inner loop runs on every change and never touches the phone: it counts the engine's work in Chromium and WebKit and screens the result with a proved rule. The outer loop runs in phone sessions the user books. It calibrates the cost model and licenses kinds of change to land without the device.

No one moves a card from stage to stage. Each stage is derived from evidence events keyed by the build commit, so a new build sends the card back to screen and voids older screen, review and device evidence.

Measurement

Count the work, then price it

Timing changes with heat, load and the device. The amount of work an engine does in a frame does not: how many styles it recalculated, how many layouts it ran, how many pixels it repainted, how many layers it built. v2 steps the page one virtual frame at a time, reads those counts and feeds them to a cost model.

Chromium · development aid

Headless Chrome in a Linux container, because frame stepping (BeginFrameControl) is refused on macOS. The page's own clock advances; animations are never seeked, so compositor animations stay on the compositor. There is no Android phone, so no Chromium coefficients are fitted.

sheet mutations · style passes · elements · layouts · paint · raster rects · layers · compositeFailed

WebKit · the target

Mobile Safari on the iOS 27.0 Simulator through the Web Inspector protocol. The model is calibrated on the real iPhone, because only the phone shows render-server, GPU and finger-only costs.

sheet mutations · recalc styles · layouts · paint area · layer census · backing bytes · accelerated animations

The WebKit cost model, per frame

dt ≈ max( T_req , W + F + U + δ ) W = J + Σ c·counts F = max( s²·Ap / R_cg , Bn / R_alloc ) T_req = 16.67 ms

W is main-thread work, F the GPU raster wait, U the UI-process apply. Every coefficient is fitted on the phone and constrained to be non-negative, so removing work can never raise a prediction.

Sheet mutations are a count family of their own. In a spike, inserting 100 CSS rules during the scroll left every other planned count unchanged; only style-recalc time rose (20–24 vs 8–10 ms). The original reads 0 after load, and fixture K10 prices one insertion on the phone.

The screening rule needs no calibration

If a variant's count vector is no higher than the baseline's in every component of every frame, and lower somewhere, its predicted cost cannot be higher under any non-negative coefficients. That is a theorem in Lean. A change that passes it is "less work" and can land without the phone, provided the counted vector covers everything the change touches.

WLess work

No more work in any frame and less in at least one, in both engines, and the same sign on the original page.

device: no
SMSmoothness or mixed

Trades one cost for another or claims a feel gain.

device: only until the class is licensed
XDevice-only

Filters, backdrop blur, toolbar and first-touch effects, heat.

device: always
PProposal

Changes how the page looks.

device: the user decides on a Try-it page

What the phone still decides. Before the model may stand in for the phone on a kind of change, it needs a calibration session and 5 of 5 blind swipe verdicts that agree with it. Expect about 5–10 phone sessions before the first class is licensed; after that, one session every 14 days plus one blind spot-check per 5 landings.

The rewrite

About 36 parts, each behind a flag, all built with MUI

The homepage is rebuilt in React 19 with Material UI 9.5 as parts such as hero.countdown, people.deck and morph.tween. Every part has a faithful variant that matches the original, plus variants an experiment can switch on from the URL.

# one part swapped, both engines, the v1 scripted swipe
pnpm fw run --preset original \
  --fw hero.countdown:strip \
  --engines chromium,webkit --profile swipe-v1

# ablate every People part, one arm each
pnpm fw run --preset original --ablate 'people.*'

# MUI vs its plain twin (styling neutrality, N3)
pnpm fw run --preset original --impl hero.countdown:plain

# in the browser
/?preset=original&fw=hero.countdown:strip
VariantPurpose

MUI everywhere, static styles at scroll time

Runtime CSS-in-JS would insert styles while the page scrolls and add to the very costs being measured. So MUI's Emotion styles are rendered at build time ("Emotion AOT"): a build-only census route renders every MUI component in every state the parts declare, and the styles go into one static mui.css in @layer mui. Before hydration the client marks every style as already inserted, so Emotion inserts nothing after first paint; in measurement builds one miss fails the build.

Pigment CSS, the compiler the user remembered, is a paused alpha that no longer builds with current MUI. It stays the whole-site fallback and an optional measured arm. Rules S1–S13 (no sx, styled or css in parts; no per-frame value through React; care with Tabs, Avatar, transitions and ripples) are enforced by lint. Spike SPK-r checks the pipeline before any part is built with MUI.

Styling-neutrality gate

CheckGate
N0 sheet mutations, page side0 after hydration, every counts run, both engines
N1 sheet mutations, engine side0 during rest and the measured scroll
N2 DOM writes, React commitsMUI equals its plain twin, exactly, per frame
N3 work counts, MUI vs plainpasses, forced layouts and layers exact
N4 static style shapewithin ±10% of the original, or a fixture parameter
N5 hydration0 attribute diffs, 0 cache misses

It cannot see Emotion's JS time or the cost of a differently shaped sheet; those go to N4 and timing parity (PL6). A failed N0, N1 or N5 is an incident against the part; the per-part fallback is Base UI 1.9.0 with CSS Modules.

Every breakpoint of the original, identically, for every part

  • Generated list. breakpoints.json is extracted from the original's CSS (media queries) and JS (width, touch, hover and pointer gates), per part. The inventory found 30 distinct media conditions and 18 edges. The Lean breakpoint model generates breakpoints.gen.json, and the build fails unless it equals the extracted file.
  • Pure 860 is not the 860 combo. A touch tablet at 861–1200 px or a phone in landscape takes the desktop path for some parts and the compact path for others. The rewrite keeps the two conditions apart, and the gate tests both paths (1024 touch, 932×430).
  • Breakpoint lint in fw gate: fails when a part uses a breakpoint the original does not, or misses one the original uses for that part.
  • Breakpoint gate before any part is promoted: PL0–PL3, original vs rewrite, at both sides of every edge, in every touch, hover and pointer combination the original distinguishes: 124 loads per engine (an estimate) in Chromium and Playwright WebKit, plus live-resize sweeps across every edge.
  • faithful-with-delta never covers a missing or shifted breakpoint. Each PR runs a fast core set of viewports; one Simulator check closes promotion.
Lean 4.35.0 · elan 4.2.4 from Homebrew

Lean first for everything reproducible

Every pure piece of the console, the site, measurement and tooling is specified and proved in Lean before it is coded. Then Lean reaches the code in one of three ways: it runs in fwcore, Lean generates it (constants, CSS media strings, JSON such as breakpoints.gen.json, test matrices), or the TypeScript/React code must pass Lean golden vectors. Only I/O, rendering and glue stay unproved.

The kickoff inventory found 87 decisions, state machines and pure functions, each at a proof level. One long-lived Lean program, fwcore serve, holds the console state and makes the decisions; TypeScript only moves data. A Node → fwcore round trip measured 17.6 µs, and 100k events replay in under a second.

Evidence, not a go/no-go

Each L1 module ships with mutants: v1 bugs put back on purpose, each of which must break the build. A bug ledger records, per module, what caught each bug. A module whose proofs cost more than one agent-day on two consecutive changes while catching nothing moves to L2 by a decision record. Lean as a whole is not on trial at M4.

Cost and packaging

About 20 modules instead of 4, and roughly $700–1,100 of Lean work instead of $280 (an estimate). The core needs no Mathlib; a proof that does goes in a separate FwMath package that Fw never imports. The browser's flag resolver is checked against Lean on every single-part override of every preset, plus 2,000 generated multi-part cases.

Generated · pre-rendered MathML (KaTeX 0.16.11)

Math view: the user reads math, not Lean

Every theorem, and every definition the user is expected to read, carries one English sentence and its math in its docstring. In the project, lake exe mathview builds this view on every build. The build fails when math is missing, a sorry remains, or the Lean (or any definition it uses) changed after the math was signed. Sign-off is an event that only the math-reviewer role and the user can cause, so an agent that edits a theorem cannot re-sign it.

Below is every declaration of the Lean core, lean/Fw (fwcore), grouped by module. docs/plan/tools/build-math-view.mjs builds it from the lake exe mathview export, with every formula pre-rendered as MathML, so the page loads no script. Theorems are shown in full; the definitions they use are folded under each module. Each entry carries its review status.

New to Lean? Math to Lean is a study page that walks through twelve of these declarations, from a one-line def to the lease invariant, and lines up each math fragment with the Lean that states it.

review pending 574 agree / 53 disagree / 0 pending

Each declaration shows its status: agree or disagree from a math-reviewer record, review stale when the Lean statement or, for rows that carry a docstring hash, the docstring changed after the review, review pending when no record covers it yet. Record for lean/: 10-17-math-review-fwcore.md. The protocol: write its own math from the Lean, then compare it clause by clause with the docstring (ℕ vs ℤ, every hypothesis, ≤ vs <, rounding, empty lists, ties, direction of ⇒ and ⇔).

At 633dda3 all 627 declarations (267 theorems) are free of sorry and use only the standard axioms (propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound), checked by lake exe mathview --lint. The kickoff sketch's 72 declarations were reviewed earlier (72 agree / 0 disagree); that record does not cover lean/.

What the theorems do not say

Writing exact math is what found these. The lease's FIFO theorem covers one release step; a holder can still renew forever, so "no starvation" is false today (default Q26 adds a cap). step_inv is one step, not every reachable state. Unit costs are whole µs, so 0.3 µs per element cannot be written yet.

The direction of a metric: lower is better (frame counts, dt) or higher is better (fps).

Every value of b is strictly below every value of a (for non-empty lists: max b < min a, written without min/max).

minRunsdefagreel.39

The minimum number of runs on each side before any verdict other than tooFew.

minRuns=3\displaystyle \mathrm{minRuns} = 3
verdictdefagreel.45

The v1 verdict: with at least 3 runs per side, the variant is better only if every variant run beats every control run, worse if every control run beats every variant run, noise otherwise.

With control runs C∈Z∗C \in \mathbb{Z}^{*} and variant runs V∈Z∗V \in \mathbb{Z}^{*}, first match wins:

verdict⁡(lower,C,V)={tooFewif ∣C∣<3 ∨ ∣V∣<3betterelse if below⁡(V,C)worseelse if below⁡(C,V)noiseotherwise\displaystyle \operatorname{verdict}(\mathrm{lower}, C, V) = \begin{cases} \mathrm{tooFew} & \text{if } |C| < 3 \ \lor\ |V| < 3 \\ \mathrm{better} & \text{else if } \operatorname{below}(V, C) \\ \mathrm{worse} & \text{else if } \operatorname{below}(C, V) \\ \mathrm{noise} & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}
verdict⁡(higher,C,V)={tooFewif ∣C∣<3 ∨ ∣V∣<3betterelse if below⁡(C,V)worseelse if below⁡(V,C)noiseotherwise\displaystyle \operatorname{verdict}(\mathrm{higher}, C, V) = \begin{cases} \mathrm{tooFew} & \text{if } |C| < 3 \ \lor\ |V| < 3 \\ \mathrm{better} & \text{else if } \operatorname{below}(C, V) \\ \mathrm{worse} & \text{else if } \operatorname{below}(V, C) \\ \mathrm{noise} & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}

Edge: ∣⋅∣|\cdot| counts repeats, so [5,5,5][5,5,5] is 3 runs; ties give noise.

A value whose position carries label f is among the selected values.

leRun means leVec frame by frame, with equal frame counts.

screen_soundtheoremagreel.136

**Screening soundness (class W).** If the screen says "dominates", the variant has as many frames as the baseline, differs from it, and under every constant term and every non-negative coefficient vector no aligned frame of the variant is predicted to cost more than the baseline's.

∀B,V∈Run:screen⁡(B,V)=ok(dominates)  ⇒  ∣V∣=∣B∣ ∧ V≠B ∧ ∀κ∈Q, ∀c∈Q∗: (∀j: 0≤cj)⇒∀(v,b)∈zip⁡(V,B): Tκ,c(v)≤Tκ,c(b)\displaystyle \forall B, V \in \mathrm{Run}:\quad \operatorname{screen}(B, V) = \mathrm{ok}(\mathrm{dominates}) \;\Rightarrow\; |V| = |B| \ \land\ V \ne B \ \land\ \forall \kappa \in \mathbb{Q},\ \forall c \in \mathbb{Q}^{*}:\ (\forall j:\ 0 \le c_j) \Rightarrow \forall (v, b) \in \operatorname{zip}(V, B):\ T_{\kappa, c}(v) \le T_{\kappa, c}(b)
screen_worsetheoremagreel.158

The mirror image: if the screen says "worse", no aligned frame of the baseline is predicted to cost more than the variant's, under every constant term and non-negative coefficients.

∀B,V∈Run:screen⁡(B,V)=ok(worse)  ⇒  ∣B∣=∣V∣ ∧ V≠B ∧ ∀κ∈Q, ∀c∈Q∗: (∀j: 0≤cj)⇒∀(b,v)∈zip⁡(B,V): Tκ,c(b)≤Tκ,c(v)\displaystyle \forall B, V \in \mathrm{Run}:\quad \operatorname{screen}(B, V) = \mathrm{ok}(\mathrm{worse}) \;\Rightarrow\; |B| = |V| \ \land\ V \ne B \ \land\ \forall \kappa \in \mathbb{Q},\ \forall c \in \mathbb{Q}^{*}:\ (\forall j:\ 0 \le c_j) \Rightarrow \forall (b, v) \in \operatorname{zip}(B, V):\ T_{\kappa, c}(b) \le T_{\kappa, c}(v)

gateOk⁡(c)=true  ⟺  {c.signedBy=lead ∧ c.attribution=namedif c.closes=Dc.signedBy=reviewerif c.closes=Vc.signedBy=leadif c.closes=Lc.signedBy=ownerif c.closes∈{R,I,F}\displaystyle \operatorname{gateOk}(c) = \mathrm{true} \iff \begin{cases} c.\mathit{signedBy} = \mathrm{lead} \ \land\ c.\mathit{attribution} = \mathrm{named} & \text{if } c.\mathit{closes} = D \\ c.\mathit{signedBy} = \mathrm{reviewer} & \text{if } c.\mathit{closes} = V \\ c.\mathit{signedBy} = \mathrm{lead} & \text{if } c.\mathit{closes} = L \\ c.\mathit{signedBy} = \mathrm{owner} & \text{if } c.\mathit{closes} \in \{R, I, F\} \end{cases}
Topicinductiveagreel.72

A topic: its current stage and the cards that closed earlier stages (newest first).

Topic=Stage×Card∗,t0=(R,[ ])\displaystyle \mathrm{Topic} = \mathrm{Stage} \times \mathrm{Card}^{*}, \qquad t_0 = (R, [\,])
advancedefagreel.81

Advance a topic with a card: the card must close the current stage and pass its gate, and the topic moves one stage on; LL is terminal.

Lease

Device lease (one exclusive resource, FIFO queue, time-bounded holds)Fw/Spec/Lease.lean · 6 theorems · 8 definitions · 14/14 reviewed
inv_inittheoremagreel.140

The empty state satisfies the invariant.

Inv⁡(s0),s0=(⊥,[ ])\displaystyle \operatorname{Inv}(s_0), \qquad s_0 = (\bot, [\,])
promote_invtheoremagreel.146

Promoting from a duplicate-free queue gives a state that satisfies the invariant.

∀now,ttl∈N, ∀Q∈Owner∗:Q has no repeated owner  ⇒  Inv⁡(promote⁡(now,ttl,Q))\displaystyle \forall \mathit{now}, \mathit{ttl} \in \mathbb{N},\ \forall Q \in \mathrm{Owner}^{*}:\quad Q \text{ has no repeated owner} \;\Rightarrow\; \operatorname{Inv}\big(\operatorname{promote}(\mathit{now}, \mathit{ttl}, Q)\big)
step_invtheoremagreel.161

Every command keeps the invariant (one step).

∀s∈State, ∀c∈Cmd:Inv⁡(s)  ⇒  Inv⁡(step(s,c)1)\displaystyle \forall s \in \mathrm{State},\ \forall c \in \mathrm{Cmd}:\quad \operatorname{Inv}(s) \;\Rightarrow\; \operatorname{Inv}\big(\mathrm{step}(s, c)_1\big)
requeue_keeps_placetheoremagreel.225

I-113: a waiter that asks again keeps its place (the state does not change).

∀s∈State, ∀l∈Lease, ∀o∈Owner, ∀now,ttl∈N:s.holder=l ∧ l.owner≠o ∧ o∈s.queue  ⇒  step(s,acquire(o,now,ttl))1=s\displaystyle \forall s \in \mathrm{State},\ \forall l \in \mathrm{Lease},\ \forall o \in \mathrm{Owner},\ \forall \mathit{now}, \mathit{ttl} \in \mathbb{N}:\quad s.\mathit{holder} = l \ \land\ l.\mathit{owner} \ne o \ \land\ o \in s.\mathit{queue} \;\Rightarrow\; \mathrm{step}\big(s, \mathrm{acquire}(o, \mathit{now}, \mathit{ttl})\big)_1 = s
renew_never_shortenstheoremagreel.234

I-091: the holder's renew never moves its expiry earlier.

∀s∈State, ∀l∈Lease, ∀now,ttl∈N:s.holder=l  ⇒  ∃l′: step(s,renew(l.owner,now,ttl))1.holder=l′ ∧ l.expires≤l′.expires\displaystyle \forall s \in \mathrm{State},\ \forall l \in \mathrm{Lease},\ \forall \mathit{now}, \mathit{ttl} \in \mathbb{N}:\quad s.\mathit{holder} = l \;\Rightarrow\; \exists l':\ \mathrm{step}\big(s, \mathrm{renew}(l.\mathit{owner}, \mathit{now}, \mathit{ttl})\big)_1.\mathit{holder} = l' \ \land\ l.\mathit{expires} \le l'.\mathit{expires}
release_fifotheoremagreel.242

FIFO for one release step: when the holder releases, the head of the queue gets the device for ttl seconds and every other waiter moves up exactly one place (this is not a starvation-freedom theorem: a holder may renew forever, gap G4).

∀s∈State, ∀l∈Lease, ∀o∈Owner, ∀q∈Owner∗, ∀now,ttl∈N:s.holder=l ∧ s.queue=o::q  ⇒  step(s,release(l.owner,now,ttl))1=((o, now+ttl), q)\displaystyle \forall s \in \mathrm{State},\ \forall l \in \mathrm{Lease},\ \forall o \in \mathrm{Owner},\ \forall q \in \mathrm{Owner}^{*},\ \forall \mathit{now}, \mathit{ttl} \in \mathbb{N}:\quad s.\mathit{holder} = l \ \land\ s.\mathit{queue} = o :: q \;\Rightarrow\; \mathrm{step}\big(s, \mathrm{release}(l.\mathit{owner}, \mathit{now}, \mathit{ttl})\big)_1 = \big((o,\ \mathit{now} + \mathit{ttl}),\ q\big)
Definitions used (8)
Ownerdefagreel.15

An owner (a client of the device) is named by a string.

Owner=strings\displaystyle \mathrm{Owner} = \text{strings}
Leaseinductiveagreel.21

A lease: who holds the device and until when (seconds since epoch).

Lease=Owner×N,l=(l.owner, l.expires)\displaystyle \mathrm{Lease} = \mathrm{Owner} \times \mathbb{N}, \qquad l = (l.\mathit{owner},\ l.\mathit{expires})
Stateinductiveagreel.30

The lease state: at most one holder (by type) and a queue of waiting owners.

State=Lease⊥×Owner∗,s=(h,Q)=(s.holder, s.queue),s0=(⊥,[ ])\displaystyle \mathrm{State} = \mathrm{Lease}_\bot \times \mathrm{Owner}^{*}, \qquad s = (h, Q) = (s.\mathit{holder},\ s.\mathit{queue}), \qquad s_0 = (\bot, [\,])
Cmdinductiveagreel.39

Commands sent to the lease; now is the current time and ttl a lease length, in seconds.

Cmd=acquire(o,now,ttl)∣renew(o,now,ttl)∣release(o,now,ttl)∣tick(now,ttl)\displaystyle \mathrm{Cmd} = \mathrm{acquire}(o, \mathit{now}, \mathit{ttl}) \mid \mathrm{renew}(o, \mathit{now}, \mathit{ttl}) \mid \mathrm{release}(o, \mathit{now}, \mathit{ttl}) \mid \mathrm{tick}(\mathit{now}, \mathit{ttl})
Replyinductiveagreel.50

Replies to commands.

Reply=granted(l)∣queued(pos)∣renewed(l)∣released∣refused(why)∣ok\displaystyle \mathrm{Reply} = \mathrm{granted}(l) \mid \mathrm{queued}(\mathit{pos}) \mid \mathrm{renewed}(l) \mid \mathrm{released} \mid \mathrm{refused}(\mathit{why}) \mid \mathrm{ok}
promotedefagreel.58

Hand the device to the head of the queue for ttl seconds (FIFO, no barging); with nobody waiting the device becomes free.

promote⁡(now,ttl,[ ])=(⊥,[ ]),promote⁡(now,ttl,o::q)=((o, now+ttl), q)\displaystyle \operatorname{promote}(\mathit{now}, \mathit{ttl}, [\,]) = (\bot, [\,]), \qquad \operatorname{promote}(\mathit{now}, \mathit{ttl}, o :: q) = \big((o,\ \mathit{now} + \mathit{ttl}),\ q\big)
stepdefagreel.67

The lease transition function: the new state and the reply for one command. With s=(h,Q)s = (h, Q), first match wins, idx⁡Q(o)\operatorname{idx}_Q(o) the 0-based position of oo in QQ and Q⊖oQ \ominus o the removal of the first occurrence of oo:

step(s,acquire(o,now,ttl))={(((o,now+ttl),[ ]), granted(o,now+ttl))h=⊥, Q=[ ](s, refused("not normalized"))h=⊥, Q≠[ ](s, granted(l))h=l, l.owner=o(s, queued(idx⁡Q(o)))h=l, l.owner≠o, o∈Q((l, Q+ ⁣ ⁣+[o]), queued(∣Q∣))h=l, l.owner≠o, o∉Q\displaystyle \mathrm{step}\big(s, \mathrm{acquire}(o, \mathit{now}, \mathit{ttl})\big) = \begin{cases} \big(((o, \mathit{now} + \mathit{ttl}), [\,]),\ \mathrm{granted}(o, \mathit{now} + \mathit{ttl})\big) & h = \bot,\ Q = [\,] \\ (s,\ \mathrm{refused}(\texttt{"not normalized"})) & h = \bot,\ Q \ne [\,] \\ (s,\ \mathrm{granted}(l)) & h = l,\ l.\mathit{owner} = o \\ (s,\ \mathrm{queued}(\operatorname{idx}_Q(o))) & h = l,\ l.\mathit{owner} \ne o,\ o \in Q \\ \big((l,\ Q \mathbin{+\!\!+} [o]),\ \mathrm{queued}(|Q|)\big) & h = l,\ l.\mathit{owner} \ne o,\ o \notin Q \end{cases}
step(s,renew(o,now,ttl))={((l′,Q), renewed(l′)), l′=(o, max⁡(l.expires, now+ttl))h=l, l.owner=o(s, refused("not the holder"))otherwise\displaystyle \mathrm{step}\big(s, \mathrm{renew}(o, \mathit{now}, \mathit{ttl})\big) = \begin{cases} \big((l', Q),\ \mathrm{renewed}(l')\big),\ l' = (o,\ \max(l.\mathit{expires},\ \mathit{now} + \mathit{ttl})) & h = l,\ l.\mathit{owner} = o \\ (s,\ \mathrm{refused}(\texttt{"not the holder"})) & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}
step(s,release(o,now,ttl))={(promote⁡(now,ttl,Q), released)h=l, l.owner=o((l, Q⊖o), ok)h=l, l.owner≠o(s, ok)h=⊥\displaystyle \mathrm{step}\big(s, \mathrm{release}(o, \mathit{now}, \mathit{ttl})\big) = \begin{cases} (\operatorname{promote}(\mathit{now}, \mathit{ttl}, Q),\ \mathrm{released}) & h = l,\ l.\mathit{owner} = o \\ \big((l,\ Q \ominus o),\ \mathrm{ok}\big) & h = l,\ l.\mathit{owner} \ne o \\ (s,\ \mathrm{ok}) & h = \bot \end{cases}
step(s,tick(now,ttl))={(promote⁡(now,ttl,Q), ok)h=l, l.expires≤now(s, ok)otherwise\displaystyle \mathrm{step}\big(s, \mathrm{tick}(\mathit{now}, \mathit{ttl})\big) = \begin{cases} (\operatorname{promote}(\mathit{now}, \mathit{ttl}, Q),\ \mathrm{ok}) & h = l,\ l.\mathit{expires} \le \mathit{now} \\ (s,\ \mathrm{ok}) & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}

Edge: acquire never checks expiry; a re-entrant acquire does not extend the lease; a lease expiring exactly at now counts as expired.

Invinductiveagreel.129

The lease invariant: nobody waits for a free device, nobody is queued twice, and the holder is not also waiting. It holds initially (inv_init) and is kept by every step (step_inv); the corollary for every reachable state is not stated as a theorem here (gap G3).

Inv⁡(h,Q)  ⟺  (h=⊥⇒Q=[ ]) ∧ (Q has no repeated owner) ∧ (∀l: h=l⇒l.owner∉Q)\displaystyle \operatorname{Inv}(h, Q) \iff \big(h = \bot \Rightarrow Q = [\,]\big) \ \land\ \big(Q \text{ has no repeated owner}\big) \ \land\ \big(\forall l:\ h = l \Rightarrow l.\mathit{owner} \notin Q\big)

DeviceQueue

The phone job queue (priority with aging, mutual exclusion, session window)Fw/Spec/DeviceQueue.lean · 14 theorems · 11 definitions · 25/25 reviewed
before_totaltheoremagreel.47

The order is total: of any two jobs, one goes no later than the other.

∀t∈N, ∀j,k:before⁡t(j,k) ∨ before⁡t(k,j)\displaystyle \forall t \in \mathbb{N},\ \forall j, k:\quad \operatorname{before}_t(j, k) \ \lor\ \operatorname{before}_t(k, j)
before_transtheoremagreel.54

The order is transitive.

∀t∈N, ∀a,b,c:before⁡t(a,b) ∧ before⁡t(b,c)  ⇒  before⁡t(a,c)\displaystyle \forall t \in \mathbb{N},\ \forall a, b, c:\quad \operatorname{before}_t(a, b) \ \land\ \operatorname{before}_t(b, c) \;\Rightarrow\; \operatorname{before}_t(a, c)
before_refltheoremagreel.62

The order is reflexive.

∀t∈N, ∀j:before⁡t(j,j)\displaystyle \forall t \in \mathbb{N},\ \forall j:\quad \operatorname{before}_t(j, j)
pickFrom_memtheoremagreel.86

The fold returns its seed or one of the jobs it scanned.

∀t∈N, ∀b∈Job, ∀ks∈Job∗:pickFrom⁡t(b,ks)=b ∨ pickFrom⁡t(b,ks)∈ks\displaystyle \forall t \in \mathbb{N},\ \forall b \in \mathrm{Job},\ \forall ks \in \mathrm{Job}^{*}:\quad \operatorname{pickFrom}_t(b, ks) = b \ \lor\ \operatorname{pickFrom}_t(b, ks) \in ks
pickFrom_mintheoremagreel.100

The fold's result goes no later than its seed and every job it scanned.

∀t∈N, ∀b∈Job, ∀ks∈Job∗:before⁡t(pickFrom⁡t(b,ks), b) ∧ ∀k∈ks: before⁡t(pickFrom⁡t(b,ks), k)\displaystyle \forall t \in \mathbb{N},\ \forall b \in \mathrm{Job},\ \forall ks \in \mathrm{Job}^{*}:\quad \operatorname{before}_t\big(\operatorname{pickFrom}_t(b, ks),\ b\big) \ \land\ \forall k \in ks:\ \operatorname{before}_t\big(\operatorname{pickFrom}_t(b, ks),\ k\big)
pick_memtheoremagreel.128

pick returns a queued job.

∀t∈N, ∀Q∈Job∗, ∀j∈Job:pick⁡t(Q)=j  ⇒  j∈Q\displaystyle \forall t \in \mathbb{N},\ \forall Q \in \mathrm{Job}^{*},\ \forall j \in \mathrm{Job}:\quad \operatorname{pick}_t(Q) = j \;\Rightarrow\; j \in Q
pick_mintheoremagreel.141

No queued job goes before the picked one.

∀t∈N, ∀Q∈Job∗, ∀j∈Job:pick⁡t(Q)=j  ⇒  ∀k∈Q: before⁡t(j,k)\displaystyle \forall t \in \mathbb{N},\ \forall Q \in \mathrm{Job}^{*},\ \forall j \in \mathrm{Job}:\quad \operatorname{pick}_t(Q) = j \;\Rightarrow\; \forall k \in Q:\ \operatorname{before}_t(j, k)
aged_beats_newertheoremagreel.157

**Aging.** Once j has waited A·base(j) seconds it goes before every job that arrived after it, whatever their class, and none of them goes before it (a key lemma, not starvation-freedom of dispatch: it says nothing about older jobs, and a job that fits no window is never started, see unfit_never_starts).

∀t,j,k:enq(j)+A⋅base(j)≤t ∧ seq(j)<seq(k)  ⇒  before⁡t(j,k)=true ∧ before⁡t(k,j)=false\displaystyle \forall t, j, k:\quad \mathit{enq}(j) + A \cdot \mathit{base}(j) \le t \ \land\ \mathit{seq}(j) < \mathit{seq}(k) \;\Rightarrow\; \operatorname{before}_t(j, k) = \mathrm{true} \ \land\ \operatorname{before}_t(k, j) = \mathrm{false}
dispatch_busytheoremagreel.221

A busy phone never starts a second job.

∀p,t:p.running≠⊥  ⇒  dispatch⁡(p,t)=p\displaystyle \forall p, t:\quad p.\mathit{running} \ne \bot \;\Rightarrow\; \operatorname{dispatch}(p, t) = p
dispatch_soundtheoremagreel.229

Whatever dispatch starts is a queued job that fits the booked window, started now, and no queued job that also fits goes before it.

∀p, ∀t,t0∈N, ∀j∈Job:p.running=⊥ ∧ dispatch⁡(p,t).running=(j,t0)  ⇒  t0=t ∧ j∈Q ∧ ∃s,e: p.window=(s,e) ∧ s≤t ∧ t+dur(j)≤e ∧ ∀k∈Q: fits⁡(s,e,t,k)⇒before⁡t(j,k)\displaystyle \forall p,\ \forall t, t_0 \in \mathbb{N},\ \forall j \in \mathrm{Job}:\quad p.\mathit{running} = \bot \ \land\ \operatorname{dispatch}(p, t).\mathit{running} = (j, t_0) \;\Rightarrow\; t_0 = t \ \land\ j \in Q \ \land\ \exists s, e:\ p.\mathit{window} = (s, e) \ \land\ s \le t \ \land\ t + \mathit{dur}(j) \le e \ \land\ \forall k \in Q:\ \operatorname{fits}(s, e, t, k) \Rightarrow \operatorname{before}_t(j, k)
dispatch_conservingtheoremagreel.257

**Work conservation.** If the phone is free, the window is booked, and dispatch still starts nothing, then no queued job fits the rest of the window.

∀p, ∀t,s,e∈N:p.running=⊥ ∧ p.window=(s,e) ∧ dispatch⁡(p,t).running=⊥  ⇒  ∀k∈Q: fits⁡(s,e,t,k)=false\displaystyle \forall p,\ \forall t, s, e \in \mathbb{N}:\quad p.\mathit{running} = \bot \ \land\ p.\mathit{window} = (s, e) \ \land\ \operatorname{dispatch}(p, t).\mathit{running} = \bot \;\Rightarrow\; \forall k \in Q:\ \operatorname{fits}(s, e, t, k) = \mathrm{false}
aged_not_overtakentheoremagreel.277

**Bounded overtaking.** Once a queued job j is fully aged and fits the window, dispatch can start only a job that arrived no later than it (with unique arrival numbers: j itself or an older job), so the jobs that can still go ahead of j are the finitely many older ones.

∀p,t,t0,s,e,j,k:p.running=⊥ ∧ p.window=(s,e) ∧ j∈Q ∧ fits⁡(s,e,t,j) ∧ enq(j)+A⋅base(j)≤t ∧ dispatch⁡(p,t).running=(k,t0)  ⇒  seq(k)≤seq(j)\displaystyle \forall p, t, t_0, s, e, j, k:\quad p.\mathit{running} = \bot \ \land\ p.\mathit{window} = (s, e) \ \land\ j \in Q \ \land\ \operatorname{fits}(s, e, t, j) \ \land\ \mathit{enq}(j) + A \cdot \mathit{base}(j) \le t \ \land\ \operatorname{dispatch}(p, t).\mathit{running} = (k, t_0) \;\Rightarrow\; \mathit{seq}(k) \le \mathit{seq}(j)
unfit_never_startstheoremagreel.298

**A job longer than the window starves.** If the booked window is shorter than a job's duration, dispatch never starts that job, at any time, however long it has waited.

∀p,t,t0,s,e,j:p.running=⊥ ∧ p.window=(s,e) ∧ e<s+dur(j)  ⇒  dispatch⁡(p,t).running≠(j,t0)\displaystyle \forall p, t, t_0, s, e, j:\quad p.\mathit{running} = \bot \ \land\ p.\mathit{window} = (s, e) \ \land\ e < s + \mathit{dur}(j) \;\Rightarrow\; \operatorname{dispatch}(p, t).\mathit{running} \ne (j, t_0)
tick_kills_at_endtheoremagreel.322

Nothing runs past the booked window once the tick at its end has been applied.

∀p, ∀now,s,e∈N:p.window=(s,e) ∧ e≤now  ⇒  tick⁡(p,now).running=⊥\displaystyle \forall p,\ \forall \mathit{now}, s, e \in \mathbb{N}:\quad p.\mathit{window} = (s, e) \ \land\ e \le \mathit{now} \;\Rightarrow\; \operatorname{tick}(p, \mathit{now}).\mathit{running} = \bot
Definitions used (11)
Jobinductiveagreel.11

A queued phone job: arrival order (unique, assigned by the single writer), enqueue time in seconds, base priority R⋅class+rankR \cdot \mathrm{class} + \mathrm{rank} (smaller = more urgent; class: user step 0, calibration 1, X/P 2, spot-check 3) and maximum duration in seconds.

j=(seq(j), enq(j), base(j), dur(j))∈N4\displaystyle j = (\mathit{seq}(j),\ \mathit{enq}(j),\ \mathit{base}(j),\ \mathit{dur}(j)) \in \mathbb{N}^{4}
Adefagreel.24

The aging step: seconds of waiting per priority level gained.

A=300\displaystyle A = 300
effdefagreel.30

Effective priority at time t: the base priority, lowered by one level per A seconds of waiting, never below 0.

eff⁡t(j)=base(j)−˙min⁡ ⁣(base(j), ⌊t−˙enq(j)A⌋)\displaystyle \operatorname{eff}_t(j) = \mathit{base}(j) \mathbin{\dot-} \min\!\Big(\mathit{base}(j),\ \Big\lfloor \frac{t \mathbin{\dot-} \mathit{enq}(j)}{A} \Big\rfloor\Big)

Edge: −˙\dot- is truncated subtraction on N\mathbb{N}; a time before the enqueue time counts as no waiting.

beforedefagreel.40

j goes no later than k at time t: lower effective priority first, ties by arrival order.

before⁡t(j,k)=true  ⟺  eff⁡t(j)<eff⁡t(k) ∨ (eff⁡t(j)=eff⁡t(k) ∧ seq(j)≤seq(k))\displaystyle \operatorname{before}_t(j, k) = \mathrm{true} \iff \operatorname{eff}_t(j) < \operatorname{eff}_t(k) \ \lor\ \big(\operatorname{eff}_t(j) = \operatorname{eff}_t(k) \ \land\ \mathit{seq}(j) \le \mathit{seq}(k)\big)
pickFromdefagreel.69

Pick the most urgent job: a left fold keeping the best so far (a later job replaces the best only if it goes no later than it).

pickFrom⁡t(b,[ ])=b,pickFrom⁡t(b,k::ks)=pickFrom⁡t(if before⁡t(k,b) then k else b, ks)\displaystyle \operatorname{pickFrom}_t(b, [\,]) = b, \qquad \operatorname{pickFrom}_t(b, k :: ks) = \operatorname{pickFrom}_t\big(\textbf{if } \operatorname{before}_t(k, b) \textbf{ then } k \textbf{ else } b,\ ks\big)
pickdefagreel.78

Pick from a queue: nothing from an empty queue, otherwise pickFrom seeded with the head.

pick⁡t([ ])=⊥,pick⁡t(j::js)=pickFrom⁡t(j,js)\displaystyle \operatorname{pick}_t([\,]) = \bot, \qquad \operatorname{pick}_t(j :: js) = \operatorname{pickFrom}_t(j, js)
Phoneinductiveagreel.179

The phone: at most one running job with its start time (by construction), the queue, and the session the user booked (start, end) in seconds, if any.

p=(running∈(Job×N)⊥, Q∈Job∗, window∈(N×N)⊥),p0=(⊥,[ ],⊥)\displaystyle p = (\mathit{running} \in (\mathrm{Job} \times \mathbb{N})_\bot,\ Q \in \mathrm{Job}^{*},\ \mathit{window} \in (\mathbb{N} \times \mathbb{N})_\bot), \qquad p_0 = (\bot, [\,], \bot)
dispatchHoLdefagreel.189

The first version (kept for the record): it blocks the head of the line. If the most urgent job does not fit the rest of the window, nothing starts, even when a shorter job would fit.

dispatchHoL⁡(p,t)={p[running:=(j,t), Q:=Q⊖j]if running=⊥, window=(s,e), pick⁡t(Q)=j, s≤t ∧ t+dur(j)≤epotherwise\displaystyle \operatorname{dispatchHoL}(p, t) = \begin{cases} p[\mathit{running} := (j, t),\ Q := Q \ominus j] & \text{if } \mathit{running} = \bot,\ \mathit{window} = (s, e),\ \operatorname{pick}_t(Q) = j,\ s \le t \ \land\ t + \mathit{dur}(j) \le e \\ p & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}

Here Q⊖jQ \ominus j removes the first occurrence of jj.

fitsdefagreel.202

A job fits at t in the window from s to e when the window has started and the job ends by e.

fits⁡(s,e,t,j)=true  ⟺  s≤t ∧ t+dur(j)≤e\displaystyle \operatorname{fits}(s, e, t, j) = \mathrm{true} \iff s \le t \ \land\ t + \mathit{dur}(j) \le e
dispatchdefagreel.209

Start the most urgent job **among those that fit** the booked window (no head-of-line blocking).

dispatch⁡(p,t)={p[running:=(j,t), Q:=Q⊖j]if running=⊥, window=(s,e), pick⁡t([ k∈Q∣fits⁡(s,e,t,k) ])=jpotherwise\displaystyle \operatorname{dispatch}(p, t) = \begin{cases} p[\mathit{running} := (j, t),\ Q := Q \ominus j] & \text{if } \mathit{running} = \bot,\ \mathit{window} = (s, e),\ \operatorname{pick}_t\big([\, k \in Q \mid \operatorname{fits}(s, e, t, k) \,]\big) = j \\ p & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}
tickdefagreel.312

The clock tick: a running job is stopped when its duration is used up or the window has ended (the window end is a hard stop); a running job without a window is left alone.

tick⁡(p,now)={p[running:=⊥]if running=(j,t0), window=(s,e), (t0+dur(j)≤now ∨ e≤now)potherwise\displaystyle \operatorname{tick}(p, \mathit{now}) = \begin{cases} p[\mathit{running} := \bot] & \text{if } \mathit{running} = (j, t_0),\ \mathit{window} = (s, e),\ \big(t_0 + \mathit{dur}(j) \le \mathit{now} \ \lor\ e \le \mathit{now}\big) \\ p & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}

ArtifactKey

Artifact cache keys (soundness and minimal invalidation)Fw/Spec/ArtifactKey.lean · 6 theorems · 9 definitions · 15/15 reviewed
stale_ifftheoremagreel.45

**Minimal invalidation.** Changing input i to a new value changes the key of a iff a depends on i.

∀v,i,w,a:w≠v(i)  ⇒  (key⁡v(a)≠key⁡v[i↦w](a)  ⟺  i∈deps(a))\displaystyle \forall v, i, w, a:\quad w \ne v(i) \;\Rightarrow\; \Big(\operatorname{key}_v(a) \ne \operatorname{key}_{v[i \mapsto w]}(a) \iff i \in \mathit{deps}(a)\Big)
stale_spectheoremagreel.73

The stale set is exactly the artifacts whose key changes: no more, no less.

∀v,i,w,As,a:w≠v(i)  ⇒  (a∈stale⁡(As,i)  ⟺  a∈As ∧ key⁡v(a)≠key⁡v[i↦w](a))\displaystyle \forall v, i, w, As, a:\quad w \ne v(i) \;\Rightarrow\; \Big(a \in \operatorname{stale}(As, i) \iff a \in As \ \land\ \operatorname{key}_v(a) \ne \operatorname{key}_{v[i \mapsto w]}(a)\Big)
dec_enctheoremagreel.105

Decoding inverts encoding, given enough fuel.

∀xs∈(N∗)∗, ∀f∈N:∣xs∣≤f  ⇒  dec⁡(f,enc⁡(xs))=xs\displaystyle \forall xs \in (\mathbb{N}^{*})^{*},\ \forall f \in \mathbb{N}:\quad |xs| \le f \;\Rightarrow\; \operatorname{dec}(f, \operatorname{enc}(xs)) = xs
enc_injtheoremagreel.122

**Soundness of the key encoding**: two field lists with the same encoding are equal.

∀xs,ys∈(N∗)∗:enc⁡(xs)=enc⁡(ys)  ⇒  xs=ys\displaystyle \forall xs, ys \in (\mathbb{N}^{*})^{*}:\quad \operatorname{enc}(xs) = \operatorname{enc}(ys) \;\Rightarrow\; xs = ys
fields_injtheoremagreel.139

Flattening loses nothing.

∀k,k′∈(Input×Val)∗:fields⁡(k)=fields⁡(k′)  ⇒  k=k′\displaystyle \forall k, k' \in (\mathrm{Input} \times \mathrm{Val})^{*}:\quad \operatorname{fields}(k) = \operatorname{fields}(k') \;\Rightarrow\; k = k'
key_soundtheoremagreel.152

Equal encoded keys mean the two artifacts saw exactly the same inputs with the same values.

∀v,v′:Input→Val, ∀a,b∈Artifact:enc⁡(fields⁡(key⁡v(a)))=enc⁡(fields⁡(key⁡v′(b)))  ⇒  deps(a)=deps(b) ∧ ∀i∈deps(a): v(i)=v′(i)\displaystyle \forall v, v' : \mathrm{Input} \to \mathrm{Val},\ \forall a, b \in \mathrm{Artifact}:\quad \operatorname{enc}\big(\operatorname{fields}(\operatorname{key}_v(a))\big) =\operatorname{enc}\big(\operatorname{fields}(\operatorname{key}_{v'}(b))\big) \;\Rightarrow\; \mathit{deps}(a) = \mathit{deps}(b) \ \land\ \forall i \in \mathit{deps}(a):\ v(i) = v'(i)

step_seentheoremagreel.520

A seen key is a no-op, reported as a duplicate.

An actor outside the MAY table is refused with the table's reason.

only_user_answerstheoremagreel.605

Only the user answers or starts steps: an answer or start from anyone else changes nothing.

cardRefusal⁡(c,b)={L if landed; "already approved" if approved; ⊥b=cardApproveL if landed; ⊥b=cardBuild or cardLandedL if landed; Σ if head≠sha; ⊥ if pass; "failed screen does not advance the card"b=cardScreen(⋅,sha,pass)L if landed; Σ if head≠sha;texttt"reviewerownsorbuiltthiscard" if r=owner∨r∈builders; ⊥ if ok; "rejected review does not advance the card"b=cardReview(⋅,sha,r,ok)L if landed; Σ if head≠sha;bot if better; "not better: device evidence not recorded"b=cardSwipe(⋅,sha,better)L if landed; Σ if head≠sha;bot if ready⁡(c); "card is not land-ready"b=cardLandRequest(⋅,sha)⊥any other body\displaystyle \operatorname{cardRefusal}(c, b) = \begin{cases} L \text{ if } \mathit{landed};\ \texttt{"already approved"} \text{ if } \mathit{approved};\ \bot & b = \mathrm{cardApprove} \\ L \text{ if } \mathit{landed};\ \bot & b = \mathrm{cardBuild} \text{ or } \mathrm{cardLanded} \\ L \text{ if } \mathit{landed};\ \Sigma \text{ if } \mathit{head} \ne \mathit{sha};\ \bot \text{ if } \mathit{pass};\ \texttt{"failed screen does not advance the card"} & b = \mathrm{cardScreen}(\cdot, \mathit{sha}, \mathit{pass}) \\ L \text{ if } \mathit{landed};\ \Sigma \text{ if } \mathit{head} \ne \mathit{sha};\\texttt{"reviewer owns or built this card"} \text{ if } r = \mathit{owner} \lor r \in \mathit{builders};\ \bot \text{ if } \mathit{ok};\ \texttt{"rejected review does not advance the card"} & b = \mathrm{cardReview}(\cdot, \mathit{sha}, r, \mathit{ok}) \\ L \text{ if } \mathit{landed};\ \Sigma \text{ if } \mathit{head} \ne \mathit{sha};\\bot \text{ if } \mathit{better};\ \texttt{"not better: device evidence not recorded"} & b = \mathrm{cardSwipe}(\cdot, \mathit{sha}, \mathit{better}) \\ L \text{ if } \mathit{landed};\ \Sigma \text{ if } \mathit{head} \ne \mathit{sha};\\bot \text{ if } \operatorname{ready}(c);\ \texttt{"card is not land-ready"} & b = \mathrm{cardLandRequest}(\cdot, \mathit{sha}) \\ \bot & \text{any other body} \end{cases}

r.\mathit{status} = \mathrm{running};\ \texttt{"run already finished"} & b = \mathrm{runFinish}(\mathit{run}, \cdot) \\ \texttt{"no such card"} \text{ if unknown};\ \operatorname{cardRefusal}(c, b) & stepdefagreel.466

The reducer step: a seen key is a no-op duplicate; a refused event leaves the state untouched (its key is **not** marked seen); an accepted event is applied and its key put first in the seen list.

step⁡(σ,e)={(σ, accepted(true))key(e)∈S(σ, refused(w))else if check⁡(σ,e)=w(accept⁡(σ,e)[S:=key(e)::S], accepted(false))otherwise\displaystyle \operatorname{step}(\sigma, e) = \begin{cases} (\sigma,\ \mathrm{accepted}(\mathrm{true})) & \mathit{key}(e) \in S \\ (\sigma,\ \mathrm{refused}(w)) & \text{else if } \operatorname{check}(\sigma, e) = w \\ \big(\operatorname{accept}(\sigma, e)[S := \mathit{key}(e) :: S],\ \mathrm{accepted}(\mathrm{false})\big) & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}

The card invariant: a landing without a violation was ready; a pending land request is held only by a ready card; the recorded reviewer neither owns the card nor built on it.

CardInv⁡(c)  ⟺  (landed∧¬violation⇒ready⁡(c)) ∧ (landReq≠⊥∧¬landed⇒ready⁡(c)) ∧ (∀r: reviewedBy=r⇒r≠owner∧r∉builders)\displaystyle \operatorname{CardInv}(c) \iff \big(\mathit{landed} \land \neg\mathit{violation} \Rightarrow \operatorname{ready}(c)\big) \ \land\ \big(\mathit{landReq} \ne \bot \land \neg\mathit{landed} \Rightarrow \operatorname{ready}(c)\big) \ \land\ \big(\forall r:\ \mathit{reviewedBy} = r \Rightarrow r \ne \mathit{owner} \land r \notin \mathit{builders}\big)

The board: a projection of the console state (every field derived, nothing stored)Fw/Board.lean · 4 theorems · 9 definitions · 13/13 reviewed
landed_not_staletheoremagreel.140

A landed card is never stale.

∀σ, ∀now∈N, ∀c:c.landed  ⇒  row⁡(σ,now,c).stale=false\displaystyle \forall \sigma,\ \forall \mathit{now} \in \mathbb{N},\ \forall c:\quad c.\mathit{landed} \;\Rightarrow\; \operatorname{row}(\sigma, \mathit{now}, c).\mathit{stale} = \mathrm{false}
running_not_staletheoremagreel.148

A card with a running run is never stale (a live wait is not staleness).

∀σ, ∀now∈N, ∀c:(∃r∈runs: r.card=c.id∧r.status=running)  ⇒  row⁡(σ,now,c).stale=false\displaystyle \forall \sigma,\ \forall \mathit{now} \in \mathbb{N},\ \forall c:\quad \big(\exists r \in \mathit{runs}:\ r.\mathit{card} = c.\mathit{id} \land r.\mathit{status} = \mathrm{running}\big) \;\Rightarrow\; \operatorname{row}(\sigma, \mathit{now}, c).\mathit{stale} = \mathrm{false}
row_land_ifftheoremagreel.160

The row's stage is stage of the card, so a row says "land" exactly when the card landed.

∀σ, ∀now∈N, ∀c:row⁡(σ,now,c).stage=land  ⟺  c.landed\displaystyle \forall \sigma,\ \forall \mathit{now} \in \mathbb{N},\ \forall c:\quad \operatorname{row}(\sigma, \mathit{now}, c).\mathit{stage} = \mathrm{land} \iff c.\mathit{landed}

Every needs-you entry comes from an open step.

next⁡(c,st)={("lead or user","card.approve")st=question("owner "+ ⁣ ⁣+owner,"commit (git fact card.build)")st=build("script","card.screen")st=screen("reviewer (not the owner or a builder)","card.review")st=review("script (device swipe)","card.swipe")st=device("git","card.landed (fact)")st=land_ready, landReq=head("lead or user","card.land_request")st=land_ready, landReq≠head("nobody","done")st=land\displaystyle \operatorname{next}(c, \mathit{st}) = \begin{cases} (\texttt{"lead or user"}, \texttt{"card.approve"}) & \mathit{st} = \mathrm{question} \\ (\texttt{"owner "} \mathbin{+\!\!+} \mathit{owner}, \texttt{"commit (git fact card.build)"}) & \mathit{st} = \mathrm{build} \\ (\texttt{"script"}, \texttt{"card.screen"}) & \mathit{st} = \mathrm{screen} \\ (\texttt{"reviewer (not the owner or a builder)"}, \texttt{"card.review"}) & \mathit{st} = \mathrm{review} \\ (\texttt{"script (device swipe)"}, \texttt{"card.swipe"}) & \mathit{st} = \mathrm{device} \\ (\texttt{"git"}, \texttt{"card.landed (fact)"}) & \mathit{st} = \mathrm{land\_ready},\ \mathit{landReq} = \mathit{head} \\ (\texttt{"lead or user"}, \texttt{"card.land\_request"}) & \mathit{st} = \mathrm{land\_ready},\ \mathit{landReq} \ne \mathit{head} \\ (\texttt{"nobody"}, \texttt{"done"}) & \mathit{st} = \mathrm{land} \end{cases}

where mm is the first step ss with isOpen⁡(s.status)∧s.card=c.id\operatorname{isOpen}(s.\mathit{status}) \land s.\mathit{card} = c.\mathit{id} (or ⊥\bot), and ρ=#{ r∈runs:r.card=c.id∧r.status=running }\rho = \#\{\, r \in \mathit{runs} : r.\mathit{card} = c.\mathit{id} \land r.\mathit{status} = \mathrm{running} \,\}.

The board: the sequence number and server clock it was computed at, one row per card (in card order), all steps, and the needs-you list (every open step, in step order).

EngineScroll.entryLe_transtheoremdisagreel.54

The (order, seq) comparison is transitive.

EngineScroll.entryLe_totaltheoremagreel.60

The (order, seq) comparison is total.

∀e,e′: e⊑e′∨e′⊑e\displaystyle \forall e, e':\ e \sqsubseteq e' \lor e' \sqsubseteq e
EngineScroll.orderCallbacks_permtheoremdisagreel.66

The engine order is a reordering of the registered ids (nothing dropped or duplicated).

∀es:orderCallbacks⁡(es)∼[ e.id∣e∈es ]\displaystyle \forall es:\quad \operatorname{orderCallbacks}(es) \sim [\,e.\mathit{id} \mid e \in es\,]

Every registered callback runs exactly once per frame.

EngineScroll.orderCallbacks_registrationtheoremagreel.74

With equal order keys and increasing registration numbers, the engine order is the registration order — the original's Set iteration.

∀es: (∀i<j: oi=oj∧qi≤qj)⇒orderCallbacks⁡(es)=[ e.id∣e∈es ]\displaystyle \forall es:\ \big(\forall i < j:\ o_i = o_j \land q_i \le q_j\big) \Rightarrow \operatorname{orderCallbacks}(es) = [\,e.\mathit{id} \mid e \in es\,]

Without explicit order keys the TS engine runs callbacks exactly in the order the original does.

EngineScroll.isRead_readtheoremdisagreel.146

Read steps are reads.

isRead⁡((R,k))=⊤\displaystyle \operatorname{isRead}((\mathrm{R}, k)) = \top

A read step counts as a read.

EngineScroll.isRead_writetheoremdisagreel.149

Write steps are not reads.

isRead⁡((W,k))=⊥\displaystyle \operatorname{isRead}((\mathrm{W}, k)) = \bot

A write step does not count as a read.

EngineScroll.filter_read_faithfulFromtheoremagreel.152

The read steps of the faithful plan are the batched read phase.

∀k,ws: filter⁡R(faithfulFrom⁡(k,ws))=readsFrom⁡(k,ws)\displaystyle \forall k, ws:\ \operatorname{filter}_{\mathrm{R}}(\operatorname{faithfulFrom}(k, ws)) = \operatorname{readsFrom}(k, ws)
EngineScroll.filter_write_faithfulFromtheoremagreel.159

The write steps of the faithful plan are the batched write phase.

∀k,ws: filter⁡W(faithfulFrom⁡(k,ws))=writesFrom⁡(k,ws)\displaystyle \forall k, ws:\ \operatorname{filter}_{\mathrm{W}}(\operatorname{faithfulFrom}(k, ws)) = \operatorname{writesFrom}(k, ws)
EngineScroll.batched_eq_partitiontheoremagreel.166

Batched is faithful with its reads moved to the front: the same steps, reads in order, then writes in order.

∀ws:framePlan⁡(batched,ws)=filter⁡R(F)+ ⁣ ⁣+filter⁡W(F),F=framePlan⁡(faithful,ws)\displaystyle \forall ws:\quad \operatorname{framePlan}(\mathrm{batched}, ws) = \operatorname{filter}_{\mathrm{R}}(F) \mathbin{+\!\!+} \operatorname{filter}_{\mathrm{W}}(F),\quad F = \operatorname{framePlan}(\mathrm{faithful}, ws)

The batched engine does exactly the faithful work, only reordered.

EngineScroll.styleRole_soundtheoremagreel.239

Writes never check style.

sound⁡(ρS)\displaystyle \operatorname{sound}(\rho_S)
EngineScroll.layoutRole_soundtheoremagreel.241

Writes never check layout.

sound⁡(ρL)\displaystyle \operatorname{sound}(\rho_L)
EngineScroll.forced_monotheoremdisagreel.244

More pending work never means fewer forced updates.

∀ρ,as:(d⇒e)⇒forced⁡ρ(d,as)≤forced⁡ρ(e,as)\displaystyle \forall \rho, as:\quad (d \Rightarrow e) \Rightarrow \operatorname{forced}_\rho(d, as) \le \operatorname{forced}_\rho(e, as)

Starting a sequence dirty can only add forced updates, never remove them.

EngineScroll.forced_writes_onlytheoremagreel.261

A run of writes forces nothing.

∀ρ sound, d, bs: (∀b∈bs: ¬isReadA⁡(b))⇒forced⁡ρ(d,bs)=0\displaystyle \forall \rho \text{ sound},\ d,\ bs:\ (\forall b \in bs:\ \lnot\operatorname{isReadA}(b)) \Rightarrow \operatorname{forced}_\rho(d, bs) = 0
EngineScroll.forced_append_writestheoremagreel.274

Appending writes adds no forced work.

∀ρ sound, d, as, bs: (∀b∈bs: ¬isReadA⁡(b))⇒forced⁡ρ(d,as+ ⁣ ⁣+bs)=forced⁡ρ(d,as)\displaystyle \forall \rho \text{ sound},\ d,\ as,\ bs:\ (\forall b \in bs:\ \lnot\operatorname{isReadA}(b)) \Rightarrow \operatorname{forced}_\rho(d, as \mathbin{+\!\!+} bs) = \operatorname{forced}_\rho(d, as)
EngineScroll.forced_filter_readstheoremagreel.283

Dropping the writes never adds forced work.

∀ρ sound, d, as: forced⁡ρ(d,filter⁡R(as))≤forced⁡ρ(d,as)\displaystyle \forall \rho \text{ sound},\ d,\ as:\ \operatorname{forced}_\rho(d, \operatorname{filter}_{\mathrm{R}}(as)) \le \operatorname{forced}_\rho(d, as)
EngineScroll.batched_le_faithfultheoremagreel.304

Batching all reads before all writes never forces more updates, for any access sequence and any start state.

∀ρ sound, d, as:forced⁡ρ(d,filter⁡R(as)+ ⁣ ⁣+filter⁡W(as))≤forced⁡ρ(d,as)\displaystyle \forall \rho \text{ sound},\ d,\ as:\quad \operatorname{forced}_\rho\big(d, \operatorname{filter}_{\mathrm{R}}(as) \mathbin{+\!\!+} \operatorname{filter}_{\mathrm{W}}(as)\big) \le \operatorname{forced}_\rho(d, as)

Reordering a frame's accesses into "all reads, then all writes" can only remove forced style or layout passes (it may change what the reads see; that is the variant's parity question, not a cost question).

EngineScroll.batched_le_onetheoremdisagreel.316

Batched costs at most one forced update per kind: the first read pays for what was pending at frame start.

∀ρ sound, d, as:forced⁡ρ(d,filter⁡R(as)+ ⁣ ⁣+filter⁡W(as))≤1\displaystyle \forall \rho \text{ sound},\ d,\ as:\quad \operatorname{forced}_\rho\big(d, \operatorname{filter}_{\mathrm{R}}(as) \mathbin{+\!\!+} \operatorname{filter}_{\mathrm{W}}(as)\big) \le 1

A batched frame forces style at most once and layout at most once.

EngineScroll.framePlan_batched_letheoremagreel.359

**Batched ≤ faithful** for the TS frame plan, for every writer pattern and start state.

∀d,ws:planLayouts⁡(d,framePlan⁡(batched,ws))≤planLayouts⁡(d,framePlan⁡(faithful,ws))\displaystyle \forall d, ws:\quad \operatorname{planLayouts}(d, \operatorname{framePlan}(\mathrm{batched}, ws)) \le \operatorname{planLayouts}(d, \operatorname{framePlan}(\mathrm{faithful}, ws))

The batched engine never forces more layouts in a frame than the faithful one.

EngineScroll.planLayouts_faithfulFromtheoremagreel.378

Faithful plan cost, one callback at a time: a read pays for the pending flag, then the callback's write sets it.

∀d,k,w,ws: planLayouts⁡(d,faithfulFrom⁡(k,w::ws))=[d]+planLayouts⁡(w,faithfulFrom⁡(k+1,ws))\displaystyle \forall d, k, w, ws:\ \operatorname{planLayouts}(d, \operatorname{faithfulFrom}(k, w :: ws)) = [d] + \operatorname{planLayouts}(w, \operatorname{faithfulFrom}(k + 1, ws))

Each callback's read forces a layout exactly when the previous callback wrote.

EngineScroll.planLayouts_faithful_formulatheoremagreel.390

Faithful plan cost from any index.

∀d,k,ws: planLayouts⁡(d,faithfulFrom⁡(k,ws))=[d∧ws≠[ ]]+#⊤(dropLast⁡(ws))\displaystyle \forall d, k, ws:\ \operatorname{planLayouts}(d, \operatorname{faithfulFrom}(k, ws)) = [d \land ws \ne [\,]] + \#_\top(\operatorname{dropLast}(ws))
EngineScroll.framePlan_faithful_costtheoremagreel.402

Exact faithful cost: the frame-start layout (if dirty) plus one forced layout per writer that is followed by another callback.

∀d,ws:planLayouts⁡(d,framePlan⁡(faithful,ws))=[d∧ws≠[ ]]+#⊤(dropLast⁡(ws))\displaystyle \forall d, ws:\quad \operatorname{planLayouts}(d, \operatorname{framePlan}(\mathrm{faithful}, ws)) = [d \land ws \ne [\,]] + \#_\top(\operatorname{dropLast}(ws))

In the faithful engine every writing callback except the last makes the next callback's read force a layout.

EngineScroll.runs_letheoremdisagreel.440

Coalescing: at most one run per frame, and (from idle) at most one run per scroll event.

∀p,es: runs⁡(p,es)≤#frame(es);∀es: runs⁡(⊥,es)≤#scroll(es)\displaystyle \forall p, es:\ \operatorname{runs}(p, es) \le \#_{\mathrm{frame}}(es);\qquad \forall es:\ \operatorname{runs}(\bot, es) \le \#_{\mathrm{scroll}}(es)

However many scroll events arrive, the callbacks run at most once per frame, and never without a request.

EngineScroll.listener_invarianttheoremagreel.475

Listeners are attached exactly while callbacks are registered.

∀a,n:after⁡(a,listenerAction⁡(a,n))  ⟺  n>0\displaystyle \forall a, n:\quad \operatorname{after}(a, \operatorname{listenerAction}(a, n)) \iff n > 0

After every registration change the engine listens exactly when it has something to run.

HeroCountdown.remainingSeconds_ceiltheoremagreel.51

remainingSeconds is the ceiling: for a future target it is the least rr with 1000 r≥1000\,r \ge the gap.

∀ now,target∈Z, now<target:1000 (r−1)<target−now≤1000 r,r=remainingSeconds⁡(now,target)\displaystyle \forall\, \mathit{now}, \mathit{target} \in \mathbb{Z},\ \mathit{now} < \mathit{target}:\quad 1000\,(r - 1) < \mathit{target} - \mathit{now} \le 1000\, r,\qquad r = \operatorname{remainingSeconds}(\mathit{now}, \mathit{target})

While the target is ahead, the shown seconds are the gap in ms divided by 1000 and rounded up.

HeroCountdown.remainingSeconds_pasttheoremagreel.65

Zero remaining time: at or after the target the countdown shows 0 seconds.

∀ now,target∈Z:target≤now⇒remainingSeconds⁡(now,target)=0\displaystyle \forall\, \mathit{now}, \mathit{target} \in \mathbb{Z}:\quad \mathit{target} \le \mathit{now} \Rightarrow \operatorname{remainingSeconds}(\mathit{now}, \mathit{target}) = 0

Once the target is reached or passed (including any negative gap), the remaining time is exactly zero.

HeroCountdown.remainingSeconds_antitonetheoremagreel.73

Monotone in time: a later clock never shows more remaining seconds.

∀ t1,t2,target∈Z:t1≤t2⇒remainingSeconds⁡(t2,target)≤remainingSeconds⁡(t1,target)\displaystyle \forall\, t_1, t_2, \mathit{target} \in \mathbb{Z}:\quad t_1 \le t_2 \Rightarrow \operatorname{remainingSeconds}(t_2, \mathit{target}) \le \operatorname{remainingSeconds}(t_1, \mathit{target})

As time moves forward the remaining seconds never go up.

HeroCountdown.unitsFromSeconds_rangetheoremagreel.99

Range bounds: hours below 24, minutes and seconds below 60.

∀n∈N, [d,h,m,s]=unitsFromSeconds⁡(n):h<24∧m<60∧s<60\displaystyle \forall n \in \mathbb{N},\ [d, h, m, s] = \operatorname{unitsFromSeconds}(n):\quad h < 24 \land m < 60 \land s < 60

The hour, minute and second fields always stay inside a clock's normal range.

HeroCountdown.unitsFromSeconds_sumtheoremagreel.108

The units add back up to the total.

∀n∈N, [d,h,m,s]=unitsFromSeconds⁡(n):86400 d+3600 h+60 m+s=n\displaystyle \forall n \in \mathbb{N},\ [d, h, m, s] = \operatorname{unitsFromSeconds}(n):\quad 86400\,d + 3600\,h + 60\,m + s = n

Nothing is lost or double counted when seconds are split into days, hours, minutes and seconds.

HeroCountdown.unitsFromSeconds_monotheoremagreel.126

Monotone display: fewer remaining seconds give a lexicographically smaller (or equal) reading.

∀a,b∈N:a≤b⇒unitsFromSeconds⁡(a)⪯unitsFromSeconds⁡(b)\displaystyle \forall a, b \in \mathbb{N}:\quad a \le b \Rightarrow \operatorname{unitsFromSeconds}(a) \preceq \operatorname{unitsFromSeconds}(b)

The shown days/hours/minutes/seconds tick down in clock order whenever the remaining seconds go down.

HeroCountdown.countdown_mono_in_timetheoremagreel.135

Monotonicity in time, end to end: a later clock shows a reading no later in clock order.

∀t1≤t2, target∈Z:units⁡(remainingSeconds⁡(t2,target))⪯units⁡(remainingSeconds⁡(t1,target))\displaystyle \forall t_1 \le t_2,\ \mathit{target} \in \mathbb{Z}:\quad \operatorname{units}(\operatorname{remainingSeconds}(t_2, \mathit{target})) \preceq \operatorname{units}(\operatorname{remainingSeconds}(t_1, \mathit{target}))

As the clock advances, the countdown display never moves backwards.

HeroCountdown.lt_pow_digitCounttheoremagreel.159

Every number is below 10 to the power of its digit count.

∀m∈N:m<10digitCount⁡(m)\displaystyle \forall m \in \mathbb{N}:\quad m < 10^{\operatorname{digitCount}(m)}

A number always fits in as many decimal places as it has digits.

HeroCountdown.digitAt_lt_tentheoremagreel.218

Every shown digit is a decimal digit.

∀v∈Q,p∈N:digitAt⁡(v,p)<10\displaystyle \forall v \in \mathbb{Q}, p \in \mathbb{N}:\quad \operatorname{digitAt}(v, p) < 10

A digit cell never needs a face outside 0-9.

HeroCountdown.foldl_placestheoremagreel.232

Reading the digits at the first n places from an accumulator.

∀m,n,a: foldl⁡(λx d. 10x+d, a, [⌊m/p⌋ mod 10∣p∈places⁡(n)])=a⋅10n+(m mod 10n)\displaystyle \forall m, n, a:\ \operatorname{foldl}(\lambda x\,d.\ 10x + d,\ a,\ [\lfloor m/p \rfloor \bmod 10 \mid p \in \operatorname{places}(n)]) = a \cdot 10^n + (m \bmod 10^n)
HeroCountdown.digits_spell_valuetheoremagreel.243

The shown digits spell the value: reading the digit row gives back ∣⌊v⌋∣|\lfloor v \rfloor|, padded or not.

∀v∈Q,p∈{⊤,⊥}:fromDigits⁡([digitAt⁡(v,q)∣q∈digitPlaces⁡(v,p)])=∣⌊v⌋∣\displaystyle \forall v \in \mathbb{Q}, p \in \{\top, \bot\}:\quad \operatorname{fromDigits}\big([\operatorname{digitAt}(v, q) \mid q \in \operatorname{digitPlaces}(v, p)]\big) = |\lfloor v \rfloor|

The digits a unit displays always read back as exactly the unit's value (padding only adds leading zeros).

HeroCountdown.fmod10_boundstheoremagreel.269

The floored remainder lies on the dial.

∀x∈Q: 0≤fmod⁡10(x)<10\displaystyle \forall x \in \mathbb{Q}:\ 0 \le \operatorname{fmod}_{10}(x) < 10
HeroCountdown.fmod10_eqtheoremagreel.277

The floored remainder differs from its argument by whole turns.

∀x ∃z∈Z: fmod⁡10(x)=x−10z\displaystyle \forall x\ \exists z \in \mathbb{Z}:\ \operatorname{fmod}_{10}(x) = x - 10 z
HeroCountdown.faceDelta_boundstheoremagreel.298

Every face is at most five cells from the window, so each face has one position per spring value.

HeroCountdown.faceDelta_congrtheoremagreel.309

Faces are congruent to k−ak - a modulo 10.

HeroCountdown.int_eq_zero_of_lt_onetheoremagreel.327

An integer strictly between -1 and 1 is 0.

Two values congruent mod 10 inside the same width-10 band are equal.

HeroCountdown.strip_shows_sametheoremagreel.366

**Strip shows the same as faithful.** Inside the digit window (offsets strictly between −1-1 and 11 cell, the only ones the clip lets through) the strip shows digit k at offset o exactly when the faithful face k sits at o, for every spring value.

∀a∈Q, k∈{0..9}, o∈(−1,1):(∃j∈{0..11}: stripEntryDigit⁡(j)=k∧j+stripOffsetCells⁡(a)=o)  ⟺  faceDelta⁡(k,a)=o\displaystyle \forall a \in \mathbb{Q},\ k \in \{0..9\},\ o \in (-1, 1):\quad \big(\exists j \in \{0..11\}:\ \operatorname{stripEntryDigit}(j) = k \land j + \operatorname{stripOffsetCells}(a) = o\big) \iff \operatorname{faceDelta}(k, a) = o

Whatever the spring is doing, the visible part of the strip is the same picture as the visible faces of the original: same digits at the same positions (multiply by c>0c > 0 for pixels).

HeroCountdown.faceDelta_settledtheoremdisagreel.410

Settled digits: with the spring at rest on digit d, only face d is in the window, at offset 0.

∀d,k∈{0..9}:faceDelta⁡(k,d)=0  ⟺  k=d\displaystyle \forall d, k \in \{0..9\}:\quad \operatorname{faceDelta}(k, d) = 0 \iff k = d

When the spring has settled, the faithful clock shows exactly the digit it was told to show.

HeroCountdown.springStep_donetheoremagreel.502

A settled spring is exactly on target with zero velocity.

∀s,x∗,dt:springStep⁡(s,x∗,dt).done⇒springStep⁡(s,x∗,dt).s=(x∗,0)\displaystyle \forall s, x^\ast, \mathit{dt}:\quad \operatorname{springStep}(s, x^\ast, \mathit{dt}).\mathit{done} \Rightarrow \operatorname{springStep}(s, x^\ast, \mathit{dt}).s = (x^\ast, 0)

When the roll ends, the digit sits exactly on its cell, which is why the settled faces land on whole pixels.

HeroCountdown.slices_nonpostheoremdisagreel.513

A non-positive frame gap runs no slice.

∀s,x∗, dt≤0:slices⁡(dt)=0\displaystyle \forall s, x^\ast,\ \mathit{dt} \le 0:\quad \operatorname{slices}(\mathit{dt}) = 0

If no time passed, the spring is only tested for settling, not moved.

HeroCountdown.countdownMetrics_celltheoremagreel.577

The cell heights in the metrics table are cellHeight of the band's font.

∀ℓ,c:metrics⁡(ℓ,c).c=cellHeight⁡(metrics⁡(ℓ,c).font)\displaystyle \forall \ell, c:\quad \operatorname{metrics}(\ell, c).c = \operatorname{cellHeight}(\operatorname{metrics}(\ell, c).\mathit{font})

BreakpointFacts

Facts about the 30 breakpoint conditionsFw/Site/BreakpointFacts.lean · 53 theorems · 3 definitions · 49/56 reviewed
Breakpoints.catalogue_lengththeoremagreel.20

The catalogue has the inventory's 30 media conditions.

∣catalogue∣=30\displaystyle |\mathrm{catalogue}| = 30

There are exactly thirty conditions.

Breakpoints.catalogue_ids_noduptheoremagreel.27

Inventory ids and TS ids are pairwise distinct.

i≠j⇒idi≠idj∧tsi≠tsj\displaystyle i \ne j \Rightarrow \mathrm{id}_i \ne \mathrm{id}_j \land \mathrm{ts}_i \ne \mathrm{ts}_j

No two conditions share a name.

Breakpoints.catalogue_queries_noduptheoremagreel.34

No two catalogue entries are the same query.

i≠j⇒qi≠qj\displaystyle i \ne j \Rightarrow q_i \ne q_j

The thirty conditions are syntactically distinct.

Breakpoints.catalogue_csstheoremdisagreel.41

**Byte-exact CSS.** The printed normal form of every condition equals the inventory's condition string (breakpoints.json, schema fw.breakpoints/1, ids mq.*).

∀i<30. (idi,tsi,css(qi))=(idiinv,tsi,siinv)\displaystyle \forall i < 30.\ (\mathrm{id}_i, \mathrm{ts}_i, \mathrm{css}(q_i)) = (\mathrm{id}^{inv}_i, \mathrm{ts}_i, s^{inv}_i)

Each condition prints exactly as the inventory writes it.

Breakpoints.catalogue_edgestheoremagreel.80

**Edges.** The tagged edges read off each condition's syntax equal the inventory's edges list (feature, lower pixel of the pair N | N+1).

∀i<30. E(qi)=Eiinv\displaystyle \forall i < 30.\ E(q_i) = E^{inv}_i

Every condition has exactly the edges the inventory lists, in the same order.

Breakpoints.catalogue_axis_edgestheoremdisagreel.119

The width edges and device-width edges used by MQ.eval_congr are exactly the inventory's edge pixels (per axis).

∀i. {N∣N∈Ew(qi)}={N∣(width ∣ width(touch),N)∈Eiinv}∧{N∣N∈Ed(qi)}={N∣(device-width,N)∈Eiinv}\displaystyle \forall i.\ \{N \mid N \in E_w(q_i)\} = \{N \mid (\text{width}\,|\,\text{width(touch)}, N) \in E^{inv}_i\} \land \{N \mid N \in E_d(q_i)\} = \{N \mid (\text{device-width}, N) \in E^{inv}_i\}

The edges in the sufficiency theorem are the inventory's edges, no more and no fewer.

Breakpoints.MQ.eval_indep_height_dprtheoremdisagreel.381

Height, device height and DPR never change any condition.

⟦q⟧e[h:=h′, dh:=dh′, r:=r′]=⟦q⟧e\displaystyle \llbracket q \rrbracket_{e[h:=h',\,d_h:=d_h',\,r:=r']} = \llbracket q \rrbracket_e

The page has no height, device-height or resolution media query, so these inputs only affect the raster.

Breakpoints.c860_le_c1000_le_c1030theoremagreel.399

The combos are nested: combo 860 implies combo 1000, which implies combo 1030.

e⊨C860⇒e⊨C1000∧e⊨C1000⇒e⊨C1030\displaystyle e \models C_{860} \Rightarrow e \models C_{1000} \quad\land\quad e \models C_{1000} \Rightarrow e \models C_{1030}

A wider combo matches wherever a narrower one does.

Breakpoints.c1000Nodw_vs_c1000theoremagreel.418

c1000Nodw implies c1000, and they differ exactly for a small screen, a viewport above 1000 px, and no matching touch arm.

(e⊨C1000nodw⇒e⊨C1000)∧(e⊨C1000∧e⊭C1000nodw  ⟺  dw≤500∧w>1000∧¬(touch(e)∧w≤1200))\displaystyle (e \models C^{nodw}_{1000} \Rightarrow e \models C_{1000}) \land (e \models C_{1000} \land e \not\models C^{nodw}_{1000} \iff d_w \le 500 \land w > 1000 \land \neg(\mathrm{touch}(e) \land w \le 1200))

The countdown's combo is the commission combo minus the device-width arm, and only that arm separates them.

Breakpoints.overlap_c860_wGe861theoremagreel.452

**Overlap C860 / >=861.** Both match exactly on a viewport of at least 861 px with a small screen or a touch input up to 1200 px.

e⊨C860∧e⊨(w≥861)  ⟺  w≥861∧(dw≤500∨(touch(e)∧w≤1200))\displaystyle e \models C_{860} \land e \models (w \ge 861) \iff w \ge 861 \land (d_w \le 500 \lor (\mathrm{touch}(e) \land w \le 1200))

A touch tablet at 861-1200 px or a phone in landscape takes both the compact and the desktop rules.

Breakpoints.overlap_c1000_wGe1001theoremagreel.472

**Overlap C1000 / >=1001.** Both match exactly on a viewport of at least 1001 px with a small screen or a touch input up to 1200 px.

e⊨C1000∧e⊨(w≥1001)  ⟺  w≥1001∧(dw≤500∨(touch(e)∧w≤1200))\displaystyle e \models C_{1000} \land e \models (w \ge 1001) \iff w \ge 1001 \land (d_w \le 500 \lor (\mathrm{touch}(e) \land w \le 1200))

Commission compact and the desktop platform mission title apply together on a touch tablet at 1001-1200 px.

Breakpoints.overlap_c1000_wGe1001Nopreftheoremagreel.492

**Overlap C1000 / >=1001 and no-preference.** As overlap_c1000_wGe1001, plus motion allowed.

e⊨C1000∧e⊨(w≥1001∧μ=no-preference)  ⟺  w≥1001∧μ=no-preference∧(dw≤500∨(touch(e)∧w≤1200))\displaystyle e \models C_{1000} \land e \models (w \ge 1001 \land \mu = \text{no-preference}) \iff w \ge 1001 \land \mu = \text{no-preference} \land (d_w \le 500 \lor (\mathrm{touch}(e) \land w \le 1200))

The sticky desktop commission and the compact commission both match on a touch tablet at 1001-1200 px with motion on.

Breakpoints.c860_not_wLe860theoremagreel.512

**Never mix pure 860 and C860.** C860 holds while (width<=860px) fails exactly above 860 px with a small screen or a touch input up to 1200 px.

e⊨C860∧e⊭(w≤860)  ⟺  w>860∧(dw≤500∨(touch(e)∧w≤1200))\displaystyle e \models C_{860} \land e \not\models (w \le 860) \iff w > 860 \land (d_w \le 500 \lor (\mathrm{touch}(e) \land w \le 1200))

Pure-width users take the desktop path where combo users take the compact path, so one cannot stand in for the other.

Breakpoints.wLe860_imp_c860theoremagreel.532

(width<=860px) implies C860 (the converse fails, see c860_not_wLe860).

e⊨(w≤860)⇒e⊨C860\displaystyle e \models (w \le 860) \Rightarrow e \models C_{860}

Every phone-width viewport is also in the combo.

Breakpoints.deskDeck_ifftheoremagreel.549

The desktop deck runs exactly on a viewport of at least 861 px, a screen wider than 500 px, no touch arm, and motion allowed.

deskDeck(e)  ⟺  w≥861∧dw>500∧¬(touch(e)∧w≤1200)∧μ≠reduce\displaystyle \mathrm{deskDeck}(e) \iff w \ge 861 \land d_w > 500 \land \neg(\mathrm{touch}(e) \land w \le 1200) \land \mu \ne \text{reduce}

The JS resolves the CSS overlap in favour of the compact deck on touch tablets and small screens.

Breakpoints.touchTablet_overlaptheoremagreel.573

On a touch tablet at 861-1200 px the CSS overlap holds and the JS desktop deck is off.

touch(e)∧861≤w≤1200⇒e⊨C860∧e⊨(w≥861)∧¬deskDeck(e)\displaystyle \mathrm{touch}(e) \land 861 \le w \le 1200 \Rightarrow e \models C_{860} \land e \models (w \ge 861) \land \neg\mathrm{deskDeck}(e)

Touch tablets get the compact JS deck while both CSS paths match.

Breakpoints.smallScreen_overlaptheoremagreel.583

On a small screen (phone landscape) above 860 px the CSS overlap holds and the JS desktop deck is off.

dw≤500∧w≥861⇒e⊨C860∧e⊨(w≥861)∧¬deskDeck(e)\displaystyle d_w \le 500 \land w \ge 861 \Rightarrow e \models C_{860} \land e \models (w \ge 861) \land \neg\mathrm{deskDeck}(e)

A phone in landscape takes both CSS paths and the compact JS deck.

Breakpoints.gap_ifftheoremagreel.605

**The gaps are real.** For every edge N, a width strictly between N and N+1 matches neither (width<=Npx) nor (width>=N+1px), and those are exactly the widths that match neither.

¬(w≤N)∧¬(w≥N+1)  ⟺  N<w<N+1,N<N+12<N+1\displaystyle \neg(w \le N) \land \neg(w \ge N{+}1) \iff N < w < N{+}1, \qquad N < N{+}\tfrac12 < N{+}1

Between the last pixel of a band and the first pixel of the next lies an open interval that neither side claims.

Breakpoints.no_gap_ofNattheoremagreel.617

At whole-pixel widths there is no gap: (width<=Npx) and (width>=N+1px) are complementary.

∀k∈N. k≤N  ⟺  ¬(k≥N+1)\displaystyle \forall k \in \mathbb{N}.\ k \le N \iff \neg(k \ge N{+}1)

Integer probes can never land in a fractional gap.

Breakpoints.gap600theoremdisagreel.625

Gap 600 at the probe 600.5: <=600, 601-1279 and 601-1511 all fail, while >600 matches.

w=600.5⇒e⊭(w≤600)∧e⊭(601≤w≤1279)∧e⊭(601≤w≤1511)∧e⊨(w>600)\displaystyle w = 600.5 \Rightarrow e \not\models (w \le 600) \land e \not\models (601 \le w \le 1279) \land e \not\models (601 \le w \le 1511) \land e \models (w > 600)

At 600.5 px the hero has neither its phone rules nor its 601+ orbit rules, but >600 rules apply.

Breakpoints.gap640theoremdisagreel.637

Gap 640 at the probe 640.5: <=640 and 641-1000 fail, while >640 matches.

w=640.5⇒e⊭(w≤640)∧e⊭(641≤w≤1000)∧e⊨(w>640)\displaystyle w = 640.5 \Rightarrow e \not\models (w \le 640) \land e \not\models (641 \le w \le 1000) \land e \models (w > 640)

At 640.5 px neither the phone geometry nor the commission tablet band applies, but the >640 nav background does.

Breakpoints.gap860theoremdisagreel.648

Gap 860 at the probe 860.5: <=860, >=861, >=861 and no-preference and 861-1000 all fail.

w=860.5⇒e⊭(w≤860)∧e⊭(w≥861)∧e⊭(w≥861∧μ=no-preference)∧e⊭(861≤w≤1000)\displaystyle w = 860.5 \Rightarrow e \not\models (w \le 860) \land e \not\models (w \ge 861) \land e \not\models (w \ge 861 \land \mu = \text{no-preference}) \land e \not\models (861 \le w \le 1000)

At 860.5 px neither the pure-width phone path nor the desktop path matches, in CSS and in JS.

Breakpoints.gap1000theoremdisagreel.660

Gap 1000 at the probe 1000.5: <=1000, >=1001, >=1001 and no-preference, 641-1000 and 861-1000 all fail.

w=1000.5⇒e⊭(w≤1000)∧e⊭(w≥1001)∧e⊭(w≥1001∧μ=no-preference)∧e⊭(641≤w≤1000)∧e⊭(861≤w≤1000)\displaystyle w = 1000.5 \Rightarrow e \not\models (w \le 1000) \land e \not\models (w \ge 1001) \land e \not\models (w \ge 1001 \land \mu = \text{no-preference}) \land e \not\models (641 \le w \le 1000) \land e \not\models (861 \le w \le 1000)

At 1000.5 px no width rule at the 1000 edge matches on either side.

Breakpoints.matrix_edge_pairstheoremagreel.159

**Both sides of every edge, per required profile.** For the profiles desk, desk-rm, touch every one of the 15 width edges has probes at N and N+1; touch-rm has them at 600, 860, 1000, 1030, 1200; and dw-arm-isolate has screens 500 and 501 at each of the viewports 1001, 1031, 1201.

∀b∈{desk,desk-rm,touch} ∀N∈E15. ∃p,p′∈Mb. w(p)=N∧w(p′)=N+1,∀N∈Et. ∃p,p′∈Mtouch-rm. w(p)=N∧w(p′)=N+1,∀v∈{1001,1031,1201} ∀s∈{500,501}. ∃p∈Mdw. (w,dw)(p)=(v,s)\displaystyle \forall b \in \{\text{desk}, \text{desk-rm}, \text{touch}\}\ \forall N \in E_{15}.\ \exists p, p' \in M_b.\ w(p) = N \land w(p') = N{+}1, \quad \forall N \in E_{t}.\ \exists p, p' \in M_{\text{touch-rm}}.\ w(p) = N \land w(p') = N{+}1, \quad \forall v \in \{1001, 1031, 1201\}\ \forall s \in \{500, 501\}.\ \exists p \in M_{\text{dw}}.\ (w, d_w)(p) = (v, s)

The matrix hits both sides of every edge in every input mode the inventory requires.

Breakpoints.matrix_observes_every_edgetheoremagreel.191

**The matrix sees every edge flip.** For every one of the 30 conditions and every edge (axis, N) it lists, the matrix contains two probes of one block that agree on all discrete features, sit at N and N+1 on that axis, and give the condition different values.

∀i<30 ∀(a,N)∈E(qi) ∃p,p′∈M. blk(p)=blk(p′)∧p∼p′∧a(p)=N∧a(p′)=N+1∧⟦qi⟧p≠⟦qi⟧p′\displaystyle \forall i < 30\ \forall (a, N) \in E(q_i)\ \exists p, p' \in M.\ \mathrm{blk}(p) = \mathrm{blk}(p') \land p \sim p' \land a(p) = N \land a(p') = N{+}1 \land \llbracket q_i \rrbracket_p \ne \llbracket q_i \rrbracket_{p'}

Every listed edge is a real flip, and the matrix catches it; with MQ.eval_congr no other flip exists.

Breakpoints.matrix_pairs_agreetheoremdisagreel.203

**Desktop-profile pairs differ only in size.** In the desk, desk-rm and touch blocks, the probes at N and N+1 agree on every discrete feature.

∀b ∀N∈E15 ∀p,p′∈Mb. w(p)=N∧w(p′)=N+1⇒p∼p′\displaystyle \forall b\ \forall N \in E_{15}\ \forall p, p' \in M_b.\ w(p) = N \land w(p') = N{+}1 \Rightarrow p \sim p'

An edge pair varies the width (and the screen width that tracks it), nothing else a query reads.

Breakpoints.matrix_fractional_in_gapstheoremdisagreel.216

**Fractional probes land in the gaps.** Each fractional-gaps probe has a width strictly between N and N+1 for its edge N, so neither (width<=N) nor (width>=N+1) matches.

The four fractional loads really probe the four gaps.

**(b)** The two hover queries of the neutral set are exactly the inventory's hover conditions (mq.hover-hover, mq.hover-none), and inside the hover-pointer-cross block each takes both values at one viewport size.

The hover × pointer crossing: in the hover-pointer-cross block (only one of hover:none and pointer:coarse) no combo's touch arm matches, so at 1200 px (screen 1200) no combo matches at all, while at 1024 px only c1030 matches, through its width arm.

∀p∈Mcross. ¬touch(p)∧(w(p)=1200⇒⋀Cp⊭C)∧(w(p)=1024⇒p⊨C1030∧p⊭C860∧p⊭C1000∧p⊭C1000nodw)\displaystyle \forall p \in M_{\text{cross}}.\ \neg\mathrm{touch}(p) \land (w(p) = 1200 \Rightarrow \bigwedge_{C} p \not\models C) \land (w(p) = 1024 \Rightarrow p \models C_{1030} \land p \not\models C_{860} \land p \not\models C_{1000} \land p \not\models C^{nodw}_{1000})

Half a touch device is not a touch device; note that c1030 still matches at 1024 px by width.

Breakpoints.matrix_dw_armtheoremdisagreel.332

The device-width arm alone: at viewports 1031 and 1201 with a fine pointer, screen 500 vs 501 flips c860, c1000, c1030 and never c1000Nodw; at viewport 1001 it flips c860 and c1000 while c1030 already holds by width.

∀v∈{1031,1201}. ⋀C∈{C860,C1000,C1030}(pv,500⊨C∧pv,501⊭C)∧∀v. pv,s⊭C1000nodw\displaystyle \forall v \in \{1031, 1201\}.\ \bigwedge_{C \in \{C_{860}, C_{1000}, C_{1030}\}} (p_{v,500} \models C \land p_{v,501} \not\models C) \land \forall v.\ p_{v,s} \not\models C^{nodw}_{1000}

Only the device-width arm separates the combos from the countdown combo.

Breakpoints.matrix_landscape_overlapstheoremdisagreel.348

Phone landscape (932×430 on a 430×932 screen, touch) is in the C860 / >=861 overlap for both motion settings, but **not** in the C1000 / >=1001 overlap: 932 < 1001, so only C1000 matches there. (The inventory's phone-landscape.why claims both overlap pairs; the C1000 one needs a viewport of at least 1001 px with a small screen or touch, which the touch probes at 1031 and 1200 and the dw-arm-isolate probes provide.)

Breakpoints

Breakpoints of the original homepage, as decidable predicatesFw/Site/Breakpoints.lean · 5 theorems · 80 definitions · 75/85 reviewed
Breakpoints.Feature.holds_congrtheoremagreel.612

A single feature keeps its value when no cut of it separates the two environments.

e∼e′∧(∀N∈Ew(f). SameSideN(w,w′))∧(∀N∈Ed(f). SameSideN(dw,dw′))⇒⟦f⟧e=⟦f⟧e′\displaystyle e \sim e' \land (\forall N \in E_w(f).\ \mathrm{SameSide}_N(w,w')) \land (\forall N \in E_d(f).\ \mathrm{SameSide}_N(d_w,d_w')) \Rightarrow \llbracket f\rrbracket_e = \llbracket f\rrbracket_{e'}

A feature can only flip across one of its own edges.

Breakpoints.MQ.eval_congrtheoremagreel.653

**Edge sufficiency (rational widths).** A query keeps its value between two environments that agree on the discrete features and are on the same side of every width edge and every device-width edge of the query.

e∼e′∧(∀N∈Ew(q). SameSideN(w,w′))∧(∀N∈Ed(q). SameSideN(dw,dw′))⇒⟦q⟧e=⟦q⟧e′\displaystyle e \sim e' \land (\forall N \in E_w(q).\ \mathrm{SameSide}_N(w,w')) \land (\forall N \in E_d(q).\ \mathrm{SameSide}_N(d_w,d_w')) \Rightarrow \llbracket q\rrbracket_e = \llbracket q\rrbracket_{e'}

The truth value of any condition changes only at the edges listed by its syntax.

Breakpoints.sameSide_ofNattheoremagreel.672

For whole-pixel widths, being on the same side of edge N is just comparing with N.

SameSideN(a/1,b/1)  ⟺  (a≤N⇔b≤N)(a,b∈N)\displaystyle \mathrm{SameSide}_N(a/1, b/1) \iff (a \le N \Leftrightarrow b \le N) \qquad (a, b \in \mathbb{N})

At integer widths the two cuts of an edge coincide, so the pair N | N+1 is the whole edge.

Breakpoints.MQ.eval_ofNat_congrtheoremagreel.681

**Edge sufficiency (whole pixels).** At integer widths and device widths, a query has the same value at any two sizes that compare the same way with every edge of the query; so between consecutive edges it is constant and probing N and N+1 at each edge N observes every change.

e∼e′∧(∀N∈Ew(q). a≤N⇔b≤N)∧(∀N∈Ed(q). c≤N⇔d≤N)⇒⟦q⟧e[w:=a, dw:=c]=⟦q⟧e′[w:=b, dw:=d](a,b,c,d∈N)\displaystyle e \sim e' \land (\forall N \in E_w(q).\ a \le N \Leftrightarrow b \le N) \land (\forall N \in E_d(q).\ c \le N \Leftrightarrow d \le N) \Rightarrow \llbracket q\rrbracket_{e[w:=a,\,d_w:=c]} = \llbracket q\rrbracket_{e'[w:=b,\,d_w:=d]} \qquad (a,b,c,d \in \mathbb{N})

Whole-pixel widths in the same band between edges give the same answer.

Breakpoints.MQ.eval_const_on_bandtheoremagreel.696

**Bands.** If no width edge N of q satisfies a ≤ N < b, then q has the same value at every whole-pixel width from a to b (device width and discrete features fixed).

(∀N∈Ew(q). ¬(a≤N<b))∧a≤x≤b⇒⟦q⟧e[w:=a]=⟦q⟧e[w:=x](a,b,x∈N)\displaystyle (\forall N \in E_w(q).\ \neg(a \le N < b)) \land a \le x \le b \Rightarrow \llbracket q\rrbracket_{e[w:=a]} = \llbracket q\rrbracket_{e[w:=x]} \qquad (a,b,x \in \mathbb{N})

Between two consecutive edges a condition is constant.
